parts.text: Paul remembers Timothy with gratitude and longs to see him, recalling the sincere faith shared by his mother Eunice and grandmother Lois. He urges Timothy to stir up God’s gift and act with power, love, and a sound mind rather than fear. He must not be ashamed of Christ’s testimony or Paul’s imprisonment, but share gospel suffering. God’s saving purpose and grace preceded their works and have been revealed through Christ, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light. Paul confidently entrusts himself to him.

Timothy must retain sound teaching in faith and love and guard his trust through the indwelling Holy Ghost. Paul contrasts those in Asia who deserted him with Onesiphorus, who repeatedly refreshed him and diligently sought him in Rome without shame over his chains. Remembering his faithful service, Paul asks mercy for him and his household.

chapters.title: A faithful worker amid false teaching

parts.text: Timothy must draw strength from Christ’s grace and entrust apostolic teaching to faithful people able to teach others. Paul compares disciplined service to a soldier, athlete, and hardworking farmer. He recalls Jesus, David’s descendant, raised from the dead; though Paul is chained, God’s word is not. He endures for others’ salvation. A faithful saying links dying and living with Christ, suffering and reigning, denial and being denied, while affirming Christ’s unwavering faithfulness.

Timothy should avoid destructive word disputes and study to shew himself approved unto God, a workman rightly dividing the word of truth. Hymeneus and Philetus undermine faith by claiming resurrection has already occurred, but God’s foundation remains firm. Those naming Christ must leave iniquity and become useful vessels for honourable service. Timothy should flee youthful desires, pursue righteousness and peace, and refuse foolish quarrels. The Lord’s servant must correct opponents gently and patiently, hoping God grants repentance and release from the devil’s snare.

Paul warns that the last days will bring dangerous times marked by selfishness, greed, pride, cruelty, disloyalty, and love of pleasure rather than God. Some retain an appearance of godliness while denying its power; Timothy must turn from them. Such deceivers exploit vulnerable households and resist truth as Jannes and Jambres resisted Moses. Their folly will eventually become evident.

Timothy knows Paul’s teaching, character, purpose, and endurance through persecution, including the Lord’s deliverance from trials. Godly living in Christ brings persecution, while evil deceivers grow worse. Timothy must continue in what he learned, remembering his teachers and the holy Scriptures known since childhood, which give wisdom for salvation through faith in Christ. All scripture is given by inspiration of God and is profitable for doctrine, reproof, correction, and instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.

chapters.title: Finish the ministry and keep the faith

parts.text: Before God and Christ, the coming judge, Paul charges Timothy to preach the word faithfully in favourable or unfavourable circumstances, correcting and encouraging with patient teaching. People will abandon sound doctrine for teachers who suit their desires and turn to fables. Timothy must remain watchful, endure hardship, and fulfil his evangelistic ministry. Paul expects his own departure soon, having fought the good fight, finished his course, and kept the faith. The righteous Judge will award the crown not only to him but to all who love Christ’s appearing.

Paul asks Timothy to come soon, bring Mark, and retrieve his cloak and books. He reports coworkers’ movements and warns against Alexander’s opposition. Though others deserted his first defence, the Lord strengthened him to proclaim the message and will preserve him for the heavenly kingdom. He sends greetings and asks Timothy to arrive before winter.
